source_name: Agencia Brasil / Instituto Locomotiva; InfoMoney / AtlasIntel
universe_and_method: Two separate nationwide self-reported Easter surveys, fielded Feb-Mar 2026; secondary reporting, no transaction panel
observed_fact: Locomotiva report: 61% named price as primary choice factor and 69% considered Easter eggs unfairly priced vs bars of equal weight. Separate AtlasIntel report: 54.7% planned bars, 44.7% industrial eggs and 45.3% bonbons for Easter; response options may overlap.
hypothesis: Value scrutiny and format flexibility may be relevant to chocolate occasions; price/format trade-offs merit a non-seasonal follow-up.
alternative_explanations: Easter-specific ritual and promotion; survey wording and sample composition; stated intention differs from purchase; respondents can choose multiple formats.
independent_corroboration: Two different survey organizations and samples corroborate that price and non-egg formats matter in Easter planning, but do not establish a longitudinal trend.
decision_rationale: Useful category hypothesis, not a validated emerging trend. Capture Google Trends time series and public retail snapshots outside Easter; keep each survey source and denominator separate.

source_name: FGV IBRE; Banco do Nordeste ETENE
universe_and_method: FGV Easter basket price release and ETENE sector note on global cocoa supply
observed_fact: FGV reported Easter basket average declines in 2025 and 2026 year over year while chocolate and bonbons continued to rise over four years; ETENE linked 2025 cocoa-price declines to weaker demand and higher production and flagged 2026 supply uncertainty.
hypothesis: Input-cost changes and shelf-price changes may have different timing; category price movements may diverge from aggregate basket metrics.
alternative_explanations: Different index universes and time windows; basket composition; contracts/inventory/FX; commodity prices are not equivalent to retail chocolate prices.
independent_corroboration: Two distinct source families provide compatible context for a price-transmission question, not evidence of shopper response or causal pass-through.
decision_rationale: Keep supply and consumer price indices as context; validate against dated, comparable retail price-per-100g observations before making a pass-through claim.

universe_and_method: Cielo broad retail index reported by UOL; national retail, September 2026 vs September 2025
observed_fact: Real retail sales fell 3.9% year over year in September; the report says e-commerce grew 5.1% nominally while physical retail fell 0.1% nominally.
hypothesis: A pressured consumption environment may increase the relevance of value and channel differences in chocolate.
alternative_explanations: Broad retail is not chocolate; real and nominal comparisons differ; channel/category mix may diverge.
independent_corroboration: No independent chocolate-specific corroboration in this capture.
decision_rationale: Use only as macro context. Do not label it a chocolate or shopper trend. Check category-specific signals before connecting it to chocolate outcomes.

universe_and_method: Journalist visit to nine supermarkets plus municipal market and chocolate shops during Easter 2026
observed_fact: Limited outlet sample reported small Easter eggs around R$20–R$40, branded eggs from around R$50, and bars around R$5.99–R$13 for 145g.
hypothesis: Price-per-100g comparisons across formats and stores may reveal trade-offs.
alternative_explanations: Historical Easter prices; small and non-representative sample; not current price and not a time series.
independent_corroboration: No independent retail time series; this source is a single field-report sample.
decision_rationale: Do not enter these figures as current prices. Capture dated public listings across multiple brands and retailers and preserve each page as a snapshot; if pages lack dates/history, do not infer past prices.

source_name: Pao de Acucar; Super Muffato Delivery
universe_and_method: Seven publicly visible 80g listings across Lacta, Garoto and Nestle at two online retailers; delivery postal code not selected; EAN not shown on captured pages
observed_fact: Observed displayed unit prices range from R$6.15 to R$13.99 for selected 80g listings; listed price per 100g ranges from R$7.69 to R$17.49. Some offers are conditional; delivery-area availability was not verified.
hypothesis: Retail offer and promotion mechanics may create meaningful observed price differences even for same pack size; capture regular and conditional prices separately.
alternative_explanations: Brand/product variant differences, promotions, location-dependent pricing, stale or dynamic page values, no exact delivery ZIP and no shopper choices observed.
independent_corroboration: Two retailer sites were observed, but exact product identity across retailers is unverified and all observations are one-day snapshots.
decision_rationale: This is a two-retailer dated snapshot, not a price trend or like-for-like comparison: EAN is absent, location/ZIP is unspecified, promotions differ, and exact SKU equivalence is unverified. Repeat at a fixed cadence and verify product identity before comparing retailers.

universe_and_method: Public product page aggregating automated observations from supermarket online stores; product Lacta milk chocolate 80g
observed_fact: Page reports 280 observations across 211 markets and 177 identified cities from 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-26; SP summary reports 149 observations across 96 markets and 78 cities, mean R$8.89, +1.1% from August to September monthly means
hypothesis: A repeatable public secondary source may help anchor the retail historical dimension while Pulse establishes its own reproducible snapshots
alternative_explanations: Non-probabilistic online-only sample; different market/city coverage by date; product identity uses name/brand/pack and barcode where available; changes may reflect sample composition; this is one SKU, not category-wide
independent_corroboration: This source offers a historical series for a specific product, but the underlying data are not independently downloaded/verified in this capture and it is not independent of the supermarket pages used by the aggregator
decision_rationale: Use as a secondary benchmark, not raw ground truth. Verify methodology and reuse terms; capture the visible date-series rows or record summary only, then compare against independently captured public listings and avoid double-counting its underlying supermarket observations as an independent source family.

universe_and_method: Four product pages from one secondary online-price aggregator; the Nestlé Diplomata page is quarantined because search-result and opened-page summaries conflict.
observed_fact: Lacta milk 80g page reports 280 observations in 211 markets and 177 cities through 2026-09-26, São Paulo average R$8.89 and +1.1% from August to September; Diamante Negro page reports 105 markets in 7 states, São Paulo average R$9.76 and +1.5% since August, latest collection 2026-09-08; Suflair Duo page reports 14 observations in 11 markets and 14 cities, São Paulo average R$11.28 and +9.3% between August and September, with the São Paulo subset through 2026-09-08. Nestlé Diplomata values are excluded until the page summary is stable.
hypothesis: Reported price increases across two Lacta SKUs and a larger Suflair movement suggest a candidate for repeatable retail price monitoring across formats and brands, not an emerging shopper trend.
alternative_explanations: Same publisher and collection method; distinct SKUs, unequal date windows, unequal geographic/market counts, online-only prices and non-probability coverage; changes can reflect sample composition and do not prove brand pricing strategy or shopper substitution.
independent_corroboration: Three products provide preliminary summary values but remain one source family. The fourth product page's conflicting rendering is quarantined.
decision_rationale: Repeat the same products with the same source and dates where possible; verify coverage changes and compare against independent direct retail observations. Keep Nestlé Diplomata quarantined until its page summary is stable. Do not pool values across SKUs or count product pages as independent corroboration; do not infer sales or shopper behavior.

universe_and_method: Four additional product pages from the same secondary online-price aggregator: Lacta Laka Oreo 80g, Lacta Ao Leite bar 80g, Garoto Ao Leite 80g and Classic 40% cocoa 80g.
observed_fact: Laka Oreo page reports 6 observations across 6 markets/cities and SP average R$7.99, with a reported 29.2% monthly decline; Lacta Ao Leite bar page reports 12 observations across 5 states and regional averages PE R$8.99 to SP R$12.29; Garoto Ao Leite page reports 10 markets in 4 states, national median R$8.74 and SP average R$7.99 (+5.8% since August); Classic 40% cocoa page reports 51 markets across 5 states, national median R$11.08 and state averages from SC R$7.98 to SP R$12.34.
hypothesis: The wider SKU set creates a repeatable secondary benchmark across mainstream brands and chocolate types. The sharp Laka Oreo movement and reported increases on some other SKUs merit checking, but are not evidence of a validated shopper trend.
alternative_explanations: All pages share the same publisher/methodology; coverage, dates, variants, product-page definitions and sample sizes differ. Monthly comparisons can reflect changing markets/promotions. Do not infer substitution, elasticity, sales or brand strategy.
independent_corroboration: No independent source family added by these four pages; use direct retailer observations and repeat captures for corroboration. Keep 40% cocoa dark chocolate separate from milk chocolate and verify Lacta Ao Leite series identity before merging.
decision_rationale: Repeat these same product pages on a fixed cadence and record exact displayed coverage/date windows. Compare only like-for-like SKUs over overlapping periods; verify product identity and coverage changes; compare with independently captured direct retailer listings. Do not pool across SKUs or infer shopper behavior.

source_name: Pão de Açúcar; Super Muffato Delivery
universe_and_method: Two directly inspected online listings titled Lacta milk chocolate 80g: Pão de Açúcar code 1363938, and Super Muffato code 291162; both lack displayed EAN and delivery ZIP context.
observed_fact: Pão de Açúcar displays R$13.99 regular with a Leve 3 Pague 2 offer (R$9.33/unit when buying three); Super Muffato displays R$7.20 regular and R$6.15 discounted. Both pages state online prices/offers are day-specific.
hypothesis: The two listings show materially different displayed price and promotion mechanics; this warrants repeated, region-specific capture before price-position conclusions.
alternative_explanations: Delivery regions differ or are unspecified; EAN not visible; exact SKU equivalence unverified; one offer requires three units while the other is a single-unit discount; exact capture clock time absent; same-day page state may vary.
independent_corroboration: Two retailer domains provide separate direct source pages, but not necessarily independent price observations because region, SKU and promotion mechanics are not aligned.
decision_rationale: Do not calculate a brand/retailer premium yet. Repeat with the same postal code/region, record exact timestamps and EAN if available, normalize single-unit versus multi-buy promotions, and preserve screenshots/page snapshots where permitted.
